title: Perspectives and challenges in circularly polarized luminescence of lanthanide(III) complexes: From solution-based systems to solid-state applications
claim: Solid-state rigidity can raise quantum yield by suppressing nonradiative decay, but BCPL is not straightforward to report for solids because absorption efficiency is hard to measure, and intermolecular contacts can change glum relative to solution.
explanation: The review notes that some solids keep nearly the solution dissymmetry while others do not, because new short-range interactions appear. It therefore calls for a standard metric of solid CPL efficiency, together with control of sample thickness, orientation, reabsorption, scattering, temperature, humidity, and mechanical stress, and for structural characterization beyond single crystals when materials are films, gels, or liquid-crystal composites.
scope: Processable solid, gel, and composite Ln(III) CPL materials intended for security inks, sensors, and CP-OLEDs.
conditions: Comparison of solution versus solid emission on the same complex; absorption efficiency required for solution-style BCPL.
caveats: The direction of the quantum-yield change is a general expectation, not quantified for every matrix in the review.
evidence_locations: Section 6.3 closing discussion; Section 7, points i–vi; Section 8
